title: Review common-stock fair market value before a stock option grant
summary: A planning workflow for a private Delaware corporation considering a US service-provider option grant. It does not itself value stock or approve grants.

parts.title: Record entity, security class, recipient, proposed grant date, option terms, and governing plan.
parts.guidance: Identify the issuing entity, stock class, recipient’s service relationship, tax residence and work location, proposed grant date, share count, proposed exercise price and other option terms, and governing plan from the company’s records. Distinguish agreed terms from proposals and missing facts. The resulting grant record should let the valuation reviewer assess what is being valued, for whom and when, including any facts outside this Delaware corporation and US option scenario.

parts.title: Assemble current cap table, prior valuation date/report, financials, forecasts, financing terms, and material events since that date.
parts.guidance: Assemble the current cap table, previous valuation report and date, recent financial statements, management forecasts and financing terms. Add material developments since the prior valuation, with their dates. Reconcile share counts and financial periods across the documents, and explain missing or provisional inputs so the valuation reviewer can distinguish evidence from assumptions. Keep this company information in the private valuation workspace.

parts.title: Ask qualified valuation and tax advisers to evaluate current fair market value, available methods, material changes, and the option exception.
parts.guidance: Ask the valuation adviser and tax counsel to evaluate the proposed option and available methods against the company’s financial and capitalization records. Include financing discussions, changed forecasts, acquisition interest and other developments affecting value. Resolve inconsistent inputs, then obtain a conclusion identifying the valuation date, stock class, method, assumptions and conditions on using the result.

parts.title: Approve valuation use and proposed option terms through the corporate decision path that counsel confirms is authorized.
parts.guidance: Bring the valuation conclusion, proposed option terms, plan capacity and report version to the board or delegate authorized under the company’s documents. Identify the precise grant scope and any conditions requiring a decision. The resolution should record what was approved and by whom, including the authority of any delegate, so the equity administrator can apply it to the subsequent grant.

approval.scope: specific valuation use and option terms

parts.title: Only after counsel and authorized decision-maker approval, issue the specific option and record grant date, exercise price, recipient acceptance, and source report version.
parts.guidance: Issue the specific grant only after the required counsel review and corporate authorization. Match the agreement to the approved recipient, share class and quantity, exercise price, grant date and vesting terms. Obtain recipient acceptance as the agreement requires and reconcile the grant to the equity records. Link the executed agreement, authorization and valuation version so the recorded grant can be traced to its basis.

approval.scope: specific recipient, shares, exercise price and grant date

parts.title: Before subsequent grants, recheck material developments and the valuation date; schedule a case-specific refresh review.
parts.guidance: Before a subsequent grant, compare the valuation date and assumptions with current financing, operating and transaction information. Ask the adviser to assess developments that could affect value. The US regulation treats a previously calculated value as unreasonable when material information is omitted or the calculation is more than twelve months old. Establish whether the next grant can rely on the report or needs a refresh.

metadata.reviewer: Starter editorial review; independent US tax counsel review pending
metadata.trigger: A proposed stock option grant, or new information that could materially affect an existing valuation before a proposed grant.

decisions.question: Does counsel confirm this stock right and recipient meet the applicable federal exception and the company's equity documents?
Which reasonable method and, if applicable, which regulatory presumption will the company rely on?
Have fundraising, term sheets, offers, revenue, litigation, IP, forecasts, or other material facts changed since the valuation date?

stop_conditions: The valuation is older than 12 months at proposed grant date
No confirmed corporate authority or equity-plan share capacity
The instrument, service provider, or jurisdiction falls outside applicability
An anticipated transaction may invalidate a claimed illiquid-startup presumption
metadata.automation_boundary: Public tooling may only prepare and check a draft plan. Valuation, corporate authorization, and grant are external actions requiring case-specific human approval.
